    THE STEERING COMMITTEE OF CITIES SERVED BY ONCOR AND TEXAS
   COALITION FOR AFFORDABLE POWER'S COMMENTS ON PROPOSAL FOR
                  PUBLICATION OF NEW 16 TAC § 25.521

       The Steering Committee of Cities Served by Oncor (OCSC) and Texas Coalition for

Affordable Power (TCAP) (collectively, Cities) submit these comments (Comments) to the Public

Utility Commission ofTexas (Commission or PUC) regarding proposed new 16 Tex. Admin. Code

(TAC) § 25.521 relating to the Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS).                      The

Commission requested that interested persons file comments by September 4,2026.1 Therefore,

these Comments are timely filed.

                                       I.     INTRODUCTION

       OCSC and TCAP are groups of over 170 municipalities and political subdivisions that, as

local governments, participate and have a unique interest in the energy market. In one capacity,

Cities are consumers that purchase electricity for various uses, including functions critical to the

health and safety of the Texans who live within their boundaries. These functions are provided

through public funds and, as stewards of these funds, Cities rely on just and reasonable energy

prices. Additionally, Cities participate in energy policy making to safeguard the health and safety

oftheir constituents. A reliable power grid ensures Cities' citizens have access to critical functions

such as police, fire, ambulance, and emergency coordination. OCSC and TCAP, therefore, have

an interest in the LLDMS.

                                   II.    EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

        As requested, Cities have provided a one-page Executive Summary at the end of this

submission.

                                 III.     GENERAL COMMENTS

        Cities appreciate the opportunity to provide these Comments on the Commission' s

proposed new 16 TAC § 25.521 relating to LLDMS. The proposed rule will implement Public

Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) § 39.170, as enacted by Senate Bill (SB) 6 during the 89th Texas

Legislature. That statute requires the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to ensure

that each electric cooperative, transmission and distribution utility, and municipally owned utility

serving a transmission-voltage customer develops a protocol to allow the transmission-voltage

customers to be curtailed during firm load shed.2 It also requires ERCOT to develop a reliability

service to competitively procure demand reductions from large load customers.3

        As a general matter, Cities acknowledge that the proposed rule is directed at the

Legislature's requirement to develop a framework for LLDMS. However, this project should also

be informed by Texas Governor Greg Abbott' s letter dated June 10, 2026, to PUC Chairman

Thomas Gleeson as well as President and CEO of ERCOT Pablo Vegas.4 In that letter, Governor

Abbot calls for measures to "guarantee any data center development does not come at the cost of

Texans" and specifically directs that the PUC take actions to ensure that data centers'

interconnections will result in reduced residential energy bills.5 This rulemaking project affords

amount available to very large responsive loads, and instead draw upon existing program structures

and budgets to fulfill the mandate set forth in PURA § 39.170.                     The Commission should be

reluctant to create a program that compensates very large loads for demand flexibility where

existing ERCOT programs and markets already compensate demand response, and to ask

customers to bear an incremental cost for that program. Specifically, Cities recommend that the

new LLDMS be viewed and implemented as essentially a subset of the existing Emergency

Response Service (ER S) program and budget, albeit with its own qualification criteria and

deployment characteristics.

         As further background for the Commission's consideration ofthis project, Cities and other

stakeholders have many times encouraged the PUC and ERCOT to reconsider ERCOT' s current

posture of conservative operations.6 Since Winter Storm Uri, ERCOT' s "conservative" approach

to operating the market has featured higher procurement levels for traditional Ancillary Services

in a preemptive effort to eliminate scarcity conditions.7                These conservative operations have

ultimately raised energy prices.8 What's more, stakeholders have argued that this conservative

strategy is now outdated due to grid improvements, such as enhanced weatherization standards

and the launch of Real-Time Co-Optimization Plus Batteries.' PUC Chaiman Gleeson has also

        A core obj ective of the ERCOT market structure is to provide reliable electric service at

the lowest reasonable cost. As recognized above, over-procurement of Ancillary Services and

other capacity products, even if for a well-intentioned purpose such as procuring demand reduction

from large loads during times of grid constraint, raises costs to consumers and restricts the energy

market. Competitive market solutions are the best way to promote reliability and lower costs for

consumers. Cities again encourage the Commission and ERCOT to prioritize the development of

programs and processes to incentivize demand response in the energy market and Ancillary

Services markets to facilitate an equitable and competitive market. 11

                   IV.     RESPONSES TO COMMISSION'S QUESTIONS

        Cities offer a response to Question 2 below. At this time, Cities do not offer responses to

the Commission' s additional questions but reserve the right to respond at a future date.

2. Proposed subsection (f)(4) imposes a maximum budget of $54 million in a calendar year.
   What is an appropriate budget for the LLDMS program?

        The LLDMS as drafted largely resembles ERCOT's ERS. ERS is intended as a reliability

program that pays loads and associated backup generators to reduce power or increase generation

during a grid emergency.12 Under 16 TAC § 25.507(b)(2), ERCOT has a maximum budget of $75

 million in a 12-month period for ERS, but it may exceed that budget by an additional $25 million

under specific circumstances. 13 Similarly, LLDMS would procure demand reductions to prevent

an anticipated energy emergency alert (EEA) event due to an extreme weather condition or

alleviate an actual EEA event due to an extreme weather condition.14 And the proposed rule would

give ERCOT up to $54 million in procurement costs during a calendar year. 15

       Just as ERS and the LLDMS serve similar purposes, their procurement costs ultimately

will both be passed on to consumers. In order to limit the impact on consumers while still adhering

to the requirements of the statute requiring creation of LLDMS, the new program should be a

distinct service with the qualification, procurement, and deployment characteristics necessary to

implement PURA § 39.170, but expenditures for LLDMS and ERS should be subject to a common

aggregate budget. Proposed 16 TAC § 25.521 even contemplates there being overlap between the

LLDMS and other reliability services, considering it makes large load customers that participate

in a different reliability service or Ancillary Service ineligible to participate in LLDMS.16 As two

reliability products that target similar objectives, funding both programs through the same budget

is reasonable, while recognizing that each program will have its program-specific terms. This

approach has the further benefit of adhering to the consumer-cost focus expressed in the

Governor' s June 10 letter, referenced earlier.

       Under this change to proposed 16 TAC § 25.507, the maximum budget for the LLDMS

should be captured under the overall budget for ERS so that there is not a separate and additional

$54 million budget for LLDMS. This would ensure that consumers are not paying for any more

                                     V.    CONCLUSION

   Cities appreciate the opportunity to comment on the Commission's rulemaking regarding the

LLDMS.      Cities look forward to future work sessions, discussions, and opportunities for

stakeholder engagement on LLDMS.
